page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz, utilizing a single thread per core configuration. It is equipped with 128 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and features a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7a.8xlarge demonstrates strong performance, particularly in multi-core and integer-heavy operations. It achieves top-tier results in prompt processing for small language models, reaching 4409.11 tokens per second. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores fall within the top 25% of tested hardware. Memory write operations for large blocks and cached small-block reads also rank in the top 25%, though uncached large-block read bandwidth and single-core Geekbench scores remain in the average tier.

The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-intensive workloads. However, the high resource density of dedicated physical cores and DDR5 memory makes this instance highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance without hyperthreading overhead. It is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, Redis deployments, and medium-scale language model inference.

Utilizing the x86_64 architecture and the Nitro hypervisor, it features 128 GB of DDR5 RAM at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmarks indicate strong multi-core CPU performance, high-speed cached memory reads, and top-tier prompt processing speeds for small language models. It is highly suitable for database operations, software compilation, Redis key-value stores, and text processing workloads.
